newsitem.title: USA: Oldest flying reptile had bizarre set of wings.
newsitem.headline: Oldest flying reptile had bizarre set of wings.

text.p: The oldest known flying reptile glided through the air on a bizarre set of wings with dozens of bones that formed directly in its skin, researchers reported on Thursday.

The animal, identified in a German fossil in 1910 but believed to have lived 250 million years ago, was no bird, and its wings were different from any other living or previous creature, according to work published in the journal Science.

The beast, known as Coelurosouravus jaekeli, "is totally bizarre because in every other animal that flies, wing support draws on the normal skeleton," said Hans-Dieter Sues, one author of a study on the subject.

The early reptile flew on hollow-boned wings that did not evolve from converted forelimbs, as birds' and bats' wings did. Instead its wing bones were formed in its skin and were unattached to any other skeletal elements.

This idea was considered so far-fetched when the fossil was first unearthed paleontologists removed the wing bones from the fossil, believing that they must have been the fin rays of a fish superimposed on the reptile.
Only in 1978 did scientists realise that the copper-miner who discovered the German fossil was correct when he labeled it "Flying Reptile".
